differences.what: a lower front set back about 3 m left of the house, with a one-storey canted bay and a dormer over it, which the 1911 sheet does not draw at 1736: whether it was 1736's own south part in c. 1890 (and gone or altered by 1911), or a neighbour, is T-2961's to argue
differences.how: T-2961, ruled: neither 1736's own nor a neighbour's, on the lot as it stood. The 1904 parcel's south line meets the street line 0.65 m south of the house's south wall, and 18th Street lies beyond it. Through the camera this front spans x 185-320 px; on any plane parallel to the front between 25 and 35 m from the eye, and for any principal point the crop allows, its south end falls 3.6-5.1 m south of the house's south wall: in 18th Street's walk and roadway. A neighbour south of 18th Street would have to stand about 180 m off to fall in that angle, and its cornice (y 210 px against the house's 186-196) reads at the house's own scale. The print is c. 1890; what it shows there is not settled by this camera. Nothing is built for it in 1904, where the 1911 sheet draws the corner open
